text: Given a configuration item id and a JSON Patch operation replace /name, when cw_update_configuration is called, then the connector sends exactly that operation as the PATCH body to /company/configurations/{id} and returns the updated configuration object.

Given operations that replace status/id and activeFlag together, when cw_update_configuration is called, then both operations are sent in a single PATCH request and both changes appear in the returned object.

Given an operations array containing an add or replace operation with no value, when cw_update_configuration is called, then it returns {"error": {"code": "invalid_argument"}} and makes no HTTP call to ConnectWise.
Given an empty operations array, when cw_update_configuration is called, then it returns invalid_argument and makes no HTTP call.
Given the mocked ConnectWise API returns 404 for the PATCH request, when cw_update_configuration is called, then the tool's response envelope has code not_found.
After cw_update_configuration is added, tools/list still returns all 92 previously-existing tools unchanged (names, required/optional parameters, types) plus cw_update_configuration as a 93rd tool.
Against a live ConnectWise Manage sandbox, calling cw_update_configuration to rename a test configuration item and set it Inactive, then cw_get_configuration confirms both fields changed.
steps: Obtain a ConnectWise Manage sandbox/test account and its X-CW-* credential headers
Pick or create a disposable configuration item in that account and note its id
Call cw_get_configuration with the same id
expect: cw_update_configuration returns the updated object with the new name and activeFlag=false; the follow-up cw_get_configuration call shows the same two fields with the same values
